[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"MongoDB Text Search: A Comprehensive Guide"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"MongoDB provides powerful text search capabilities that allow you to efficiently search for text within string fields in your documents. This tutorial will guide you through the process of setting up and using text search in MongoDB."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Creating a Text Index"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before you can perform text searches, you need to create a text index on the field(s) you want to search. You can create a text index on one or more string fields."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"// Create a text index on the 'fieldName' field
db.collectionName.createIndex( { fieldName: "text" } )"},{"order":6,"type":"code","text":"// Create a compound text index on multiple fields
db.collectionName.createIndex(
  {
    field1: "text",
    field2: "text"
  }
)"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replace 'collectionName' with the name of your collection, and 'fieldName', 'field1', 'field2', etc., with the names of the fields you want to index.  A single collection can only have one text index. If you need to search across multiple fields, create a compound text index."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Performing Text Searches"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once you have a text index, you can use the '$text' operator to perform text searches. The '$text' operator uses a text index to search for terms in the indexed fields."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"// Search for documents containing the term 'keyword'
db.collectionName.find( { $text: { $search: "keyword" } } )"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"The '$search' operator accepts a string containing the search terms. MongoDB will tokenize the search string and search for documents that contain any of the tokens."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Phrase Searches"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"To search for an exact phrase, enclose the phrase in double quotes."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"// Search for documents containing the phrase "exact phrase"
db.collectionName.find( { $text: { $search: '"exact phrase"' } } )"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Exclusion of Terms"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"To exclude terms from the search, prefix them with a hyphen (-)."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"// Search for documents containing 'keyword' but not 'exclude'
db.collectionName.find( { $text: { $search: "keyword -exclude" } } )"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Text Search with Case Insensitivity and Diacritic Insensitivity"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Text search in MongoDB is case-insensitive and diacritic-insensitive by default. This means that searches will match regardless of the case or accents of the search terms."},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"6. Limiting the Number of Results"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can limit the number of results returned by using the 'limit()' method."},{"order":22,"type":"code","text":"// Limit the results to 10 documents
db.collectionName.find( { $text: { $search: "keyword" } } ).limit(10)"},{"order":23,"type":"subheading","text":"7. Sorting by Relevance (Text Score)"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"MongoDB calculates a text score for each document that matches the search criteria. You can sort the results by text score to return the most relevant documents first. To do this, you need to use the '$meta' operator in the 'sort()' method."},{"order":25,"type":"code","text":"// Sort by text score (relevance)
db.collectionName.find( { $text: { $search: "keyword" } }, { score: { $meta: "textScore" } } ).sort( { score: { $meta: "textScore" } } )"},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this example, we project the 'score' field using '$meta: "textScore"' and then sort by the 'score' field, also using '$meta: "textScore"'."},{"order":27,"type":"subheading","text":"8. Considerations and Limitations"},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Only one text index is allowed per collection."},{"order":29,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Text indexes can be large and may impact write performance."},{"order":30,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Text search is not suitable for exact match searches; use regular indexes for that."},{"order":31,"type":"paragraph","text":"By following this tutorial, you should now be able to effectively use text search in MongoDB to find the information you need."}]
